page.layout: Running head at top left, page number 47 at top right. One main text column, with marginal notes in the right margin (a reference "Jac. 4." beside the line with the star, and a longer note beside the lines of "y In omni juramento" through "Paulus."). Below the text, at the right, the catchword "Sub-".

main_text.p: telligendum, quin ut in omni jura-mento utcunque simpliciter enunciato & sine exceptione, subintelligi tamen possint & debeant omnes illæ sive Ex-ceptiones, sive Conditiones, quæ de jure communi subintelligi solent ad hoc ut Juramentum obliget. Quarum sunt præcipuæ, & ad quas fortassis reliqua-rum pleraque reduci possunt, iftæ quæ sequuntur. Subintelligendum primò, Si Deus permiserit: secundum[?] illud Ja-cobi, * Si Dominus voluerit & vixe-rimus, faciemus hoc vel illud. Jac. 4.Unde si Cajus Titio juret se ad kal. Januarias Londini affuturum, & pecunias quas ei debet allaturum; si ad id tempus gravi morbo correptus decubuerit, aut in iti-nere à latronibus expoliatus nummos a-miserit: in hoc casu non tenetur perju-rii. Ratio est: quia cum omnia divinæ providentiæ & voluntati subsint, nec it in cujusvis hominis potestate omnes futuros casus præstare: qui fecit quod in e fuit ut adimpleret quod promiserat, uramenti fidem exolvit. Nam cum rei impossibilis nulla sit obligatio, ut mox audietis: omne juramentum ex lege communi debet intelligi cum clausula {y}NisiIn omni juramento vel facramento intelligun-tur tujusmodi generales conditiones, sive Deus voluerit, Si vi-xero, Si po-tero. Gloss. ad 22. qu. 2. c. B. Paulus. Deo aliter visum fuerit, aut alia simili.

page.notes: The first word "telligendum" is a fragment cut at the left edge of the scan and stays a fragment. "secundum" is printed with a letter that looks like an f; I read it as secundum but marked it [?]. The marginal note "Gloss." and the citation "ad 22. qu. 2. c. B. Paulus." are doubtful at the edges of the scan and may have small errors. The "y" mark in the note is set in italic; the note's Latin is transcribed as printed, with its hyphenations kept. "Ratio est" and "subsint" are printed with the long s; these have been rendered with a plain s.
